# taba_queue (Resource)

A queue. Every queue gets a dead-letter queue (`dead_letter_name`), created and removed with it.

Changing `name`, `fifo` or `volatile` replaces the queue, and removing a queue removes its messages: unless `force_destroy` is `true`, the removal (`destroy`, or the replacement) is refused while the queue or its dead-letter holds a message.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A durable queue: what is not declared follows the node default (see the effective_* attributes).
resource "taba_queue" "orders" {
  name           = "orders"
  ttl            = 86400
  max_deliveries = 5
  tags = {
    team = "billing"
  }
}

# A FIFO queue (the cluster needs replication.factor of 2 or more).
resource "taba_queue" "payments" {
  name = "payments"
  fifo = true
}

# A volatile queue, removed after 15 minutes without a consumer. force_destroy lets a destroy remove it with
# messages in it.
resource "taba_queue" "notifications" {
  name          = "notifications"
  volatile      = true
  idle_timeout  = 900
  force_destroy = true
}

# A queue that may already exist (created by an application at startup, say): it is taken over and gets the
# declared configuration instead of failing the creation. From then on it belongs to this state, and a destroy
# removes it.
resource "taba_queue" "events" {
  name             = "events"
  ttl              = 3600
  create_or_update = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name: 1 to 100 characters `A-Za-z0-9_-`, case-sensitive, not ending in `-dead-letter`. Changing it replaces the queue.

### Optional

- `create_or_update` (Boolean) When creating, take over a topic with this name that already exists instead of failing: it gets the declared configuration (what is not declared goes back to the node default). A topic with another type, `fifo` or `volatile` is recreated only if it holds no message; otherwise nothing changes and the creation fails. Not set: the provider `create_or_update` (default `false`). It is only used when the resource is created; afterwards the resource belongs to this state like any other, and a `destroy` removes it.
- `fifo` (Boolean) FIFO queue (order per group and deduplication). Needs `replication.factor` of 2 or more on the cluster. Changing it replaces the queue. Default: `false`.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Remove the queue even when it holds messages (they are lost). With `false`, the removal is refused while the queue or its dead-letter holds a message. It is read from the state, so set it to `true` and apply before a `destroy` or a replacement. Default: `false`.
- `idle_timeout` (Number) Volatile queue only: seconds without a consumer until the queue is removed (60 to 604800). Default on a volatile queue: `600`.
- `max_deliveries` (Number) Deliveries without an ack before the message goes to the dead-letter (1 to 1000). Not set: the node default (`effective_max_deliveries`).
- `max_message_bytes` (Number) Maximum size of a message, in bytes (1 up to the node `message.hard-limit`). Not set: the node default (`effective_max_message_bytes`).
- `tags` (Map of String) Telemetry tags (up to 20; key of 1 to 64 and value of 0 to 128 characters `A-Za-z0-9_-.:`). They do not affect behaviour. Default: none.
- `ttl` (Number) Message lifetime, in seconds (60 to 31536000). Not set: the node default (`effective_ttl`).
- `volatile` (Boolean) Volatile queue: messages only in memory, and the queue is removed after `idle_timeout` without a consumer. Changing it replaces the queue. Default: `false`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation date (RFC 3339).
- `dead_letter_name` (String) Name of the dead-letter queue of this queue (`<name>-dead-letter`).
- `effective_max_deliveries` (Number) The `max_deliveries` in force: the declared one or the node default.
- `effective_max_message_bytes` (Number) The `max_message_bytes` in force: the declared one or the node default.
- `effective_ttl` (Number) The `ttl` in force: the declared one or the node default.
- `id` (String) Identifier the server gave the queue (a new one when the queue is replaced).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A queue is imported by its name.
terraform import taba_queue.orders orders
```
